text:
marco: quick UX check  proposal to reduce chart header noise. idea: single-line axis labels + a small 'scale tag' (e.g., 'Units: USD') anchored to the axis, plus an annotation-density control to avoid too many point labels on dense series. thoughts? :eyes:

tess: can you drop a screenshot or figma link? curious how the scale tag behaves with long series names in the legend

marco: figma here: https://figma.com/file/abc/scale-tag-annotation-density (screenshot attached). behaviour notes: tag collapses to an icon on very narrow widths, hover expands. annotation-density is a tiny slider in chart settings (low/medium/high) that limits inline point labels and toggles condensed markers.

ravi: liking the density control. question about accessibility: if we hide inline labels at low density, how do screenreaders announce spikes or labeled points? need a fallback so VO users still get signposted events

elaine: agree with ravi. proposal: when density is reduced, maintain a separate accessible summary list for screenreaders that enumerates flagged points (timestamp + value + short reason). visually hidden but tabbable from chart header. also the scale tag should expose full text via aria-label: e.g., aria-label="Units: US dollars"

marco: good call. for visual cues on spikes i was thinking of a "spike whisper" marker: tiny hollow diamond with a chevron for options. default is non-invasive annotate-only; users can enable "compress spikes" in preferences which caps extremes and shows a patterned fill on capped areas.

tess: microcopy for the whisper tooltip: "Spike detected — 12.3M. Options: Annotate | Compress" maybe shorter: "Spike: 12.3M. Annotate or compress." also export PNGs need to include the scale tag text, not the icon-only fallback. docs team will complain otherwise.

ravi: keyboard flow nit  ensure the density slider is reachable via keyboard from the chart header; order: legend items -> density control -> toolbar actions. if the density control is in a popover, popover trigger must be the next tab stop after legend.

elaine: color accessibility: do not rely on hue to convey spike vs normal. use an outline pattern + aria-describedby for the marker. when the marker is focused, screenreader should say "Spike at 2026-02-03: 12.3 million"

marco: action list: 1) implement scale tag with full aria-label + hover expansion; 2) annotation-density control in chart settings and keyboard-accessible summary for low density; 3) spike whisper marker (annotate by default) + optional compress mode in prefs; 4) ensure PNG exports preserve readable scale tag text; 5) acceptance tests for keyboard/VO flow and color-blind patterns. i'll mock the density slider interactions tomorrow.

designbot: created ticket #4780: "scale-tag + annotation-density + spike whisper" assigned to @marco and @elaine.

tess: tiny copy preference: prefer the explicit prefix "Units:" in the scale tag (e.g., "Units: Requests") when the axis label could be ambiguous.

marco: noted  i'll include both variants in the prototype for quick A/B in the next sync. thanks everyone. closing thread after prototype upload. :sparkles:
